'''Ian Michael Redmond''' [[OBE]] [[Fellow of the Zoological Society of London|FZS]] [[Fellow of the Linnean Society|FLS]] (born 11 April 1954<ref>‘REDMOND, Ian Michael’, Who's Who 2013, A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2013; online edn, Oxford University Press, Dec 2012; online edn, Nov 2012 [http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U2000158, accessed 11 May 2013]</ref>) is a tropical field biologist and conservationist. Renowned for his work with [[mountain gorillas]] and [[elephant]]s, Redmond has been involved in more than 50 documentaries on the subject for, among others, the [[BBC]], [[National Geographic Society|National Geographic]] and the [[Discovery Channel]]. Redmond was also involved in the 1988 film ''[[Gorillas in the Mist]]'', spending some time with [[Sigourney Weaver]] so she could better understand her character.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gordonpoole.com/?artistID=1123 |title=Motivational Speakers &#124; Business Speakers &#124; After Dinner Speakers &#124; Gordon Poole Agency Ltd |publisher=Gordonpoole.com |access-date=2012-06-25}}</ref>

As a junior researcher working with [[Dian Fossey]], he was involved in the filming of [[David Attenborough]]'s [[Life on Earth (TV series)#Gorilla encounter|famous encounter]] with a group of [[mountain gorilla]]s in her sanctuary in Rwanda.<ref name="DA90">{{cite episode |title=Attenborough at 90 |series=Celebrating Attenborough at 90 |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p03qxjzj |access-date=8 May 2016 |network=[[BBC Television]] |date=8 May 2016 }}</ref> He recalled the event in a BBC tribute programme marking Attenborough's 90th birthday.<ref name="DA90" />

When Dian's favourite gorilla Digit was killed in 1978, it was Ian who found the body. He subsequently became chairman and trustee of [[The Gorilla Organization]] (originally known as the Digit Fund, later the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund, then Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund Europe),<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pittock |first1=Jason |title=Introducing the Gorilla Organization |url=https://onthehill.info/2018/10/introducing-the-gorilla-organization/ |access-date=2 January 2026 |work=On the Hill, the Primrose Hill Magazine |date=13 October 2018}}</ref> and took part in multiple Great Gorilla Run fundraising events for this charity, walking 8&nbsp;km on his knuckles (as gorillas do).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bishumba |first1=Nasra |title=UN Gorilla Ambassador for Charity marathon |url=https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/25227/un-gorilla-ambassador-for-charity-marathon |access-date=2 January 2026 |work=The New Times |date=6 September 2009 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Webber |first1=Emily |title=Stroud gorilla expert to do eight kilometre run on knuckles |url=https://www.stroudnewsandjournal.co.uk/news/15494342.stroud-gorilla-expert-to-do-eight-kilometre-run-on-knuckles/ |access-date=2 January 2026 |work=Stroud News and Journal |date=26 August 2017 |language=en}}</ref>

Similarly to Dian's Digit Fund, Ian set up the African Elephant Fund after he discovered the body of Charles, an [[Kitum Cave|underground elephant]] he had named.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gaffney |first1=Audrey |title=Ian Redmond talks to Ethical Bucket List |url=https://ethicalbucketlist.com/blog-article/ian-redmond-talks-to-ethical-bucket-list/ |website=Ethical Bucket List |access-date=2 January 2026 |language=en |date=6 February 2021}}</ref> The African Ele-Fund was known for the 1989 Elefriends campaign to ban the ivory trade.

He was Ambassador for the 2009 United Nations 'Year of the Gorilla',<ref>{{cite web |title=Legends and Legacies of Conservation in Africa |url=https://legendsandlegaciesofafrica.org/ianredmond.php |website=legendsandlegaciesofafrica.org |access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref> from 2020-2024 was Ambassador for the UN's [[Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals]].,<ref>{{cite web |title=Migratory Species Ambassador Programme (2006 - 2024) [Archive] {{!}} Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals |url=https://www.cms.int/about/migratory-species-ambassador-programme |website=www.cms.int |access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref> and is currently Ambassador for [https://www.vecotourism.org/ Virtual Ecotourism].<ref>{{cite web |title=For the Day of the Elephants, a Crash Course in Conservation |url=https://mountelgonfoundation.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Nat-Geo-Voices-blog-about-Kali-For-the-Day-of-the-Elephants-Crash-Course-in-Conservation-Ian-Redmond-2016.pdf |website=Mt Elgon Foundation |publisher=National Geographic Society Newsroom |access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref>

He has acted as consultant/advisor to the [[Born Free Foundation]], [[International Fund for Animal Welfare]], [[United Nations Environment Programme]] (UNEP), [[Food and Agriculture Organization]] (FAO), and [[Orangutan Foundation International]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Campaigns Dept |url=http://www.bornfree.org.uk/about-us/staff/campaigns-dept/ |website=www.bornfree.org.uk |publisher=Born Free Foundation |access-date=2 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110213110234/http://www.bornfree.org.uk/about-us/staff/campaigns-dept/ |archive-date=13 Feb 2011 |language=en |date=11 Jan 2008}}</ref>

He established (and chairs) the [https://www.4apes.com/ Ape Alliance], and previously founded the UK Rhino Group (a coalition of 26 conservation organizations which staged a 'Rhino May Day' on 8 May 1999).

He also helped launch the UNEP/UNESCO [[Great Apes Survival Partnership]] (GRASP) in 2001 and was its Chief Consultant and Envoy until 2012. More recently he co-founded [https://www.rebalance.earth/ Rebalance Earth], a capital investment manager treating nature as investible infrastructure.

== Early life and family ==
Redmond was born in [[Malaysia]], moving to [[Beverley|Beverley, East Riding of Yorkshire, England]] aged five to live with his mother. It was in Beverley where his love of animals led to his becoming a member of the Beverley and Hull Naturalist Society. Redmond attended [[Keele University]], studying [[Biology]] and Psychology.

Redmond is married with twin sons, Matthew and Benjamin. He has two brothers, Tom, a French horn player, and Timothy, a conductor.

== Awards and honours ==
His work on behalf of animals was recognized in 1996 with the presentation of the [[Performing Animal Welfare Society]] (PAWS) Humane Achievement Award, at a ceremony in Hollywood.

He was appointed OBE in the Queen’s Birthday Honours in 2006.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bond |first1=Chris |title='Who'd have thought they'd give a gong to a bloke who still prefers to wear shorts and hang out with gorillas?' - Features - Yorkshire Post |url=http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/features/who-d-have-thought-they-d-give-a-gong-to-a-bloke-who-still-prefers-to-wear-shorts-and-hang-out-with-gorillas-1-2376148 |access-date=2 January 2026 |work=Yorkshire Post |date=26 June 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010192707/http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/features/who-d-have-thought-they-d-give-a-gong-to-a-bloke-who-still-prefers-to-wear-shorts-and-hang-out-with-gorillas-1-2376148 |archive-date=10 Oct 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.orangutan.org.uk/latest-news/125-ian-redmond-receives-obe |title=Ian Redmond Receives OBE |publisher=Orangutan.org.uk |date=2006-06-22 |access-date=2012-06-25 |archive-date=26 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926083956/http://www.orangutan.org.uk/latest-news/125-ian-redmond-receives-obe |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2011, he was awarded an honorary degree from [[Oxford Brookes University]] for his conservation work.

In 2013 he received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the New York [[Wildlife Conservation Film Festival]], and also the IFAW Animal Action Award for Conservation.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Conversation With Ian Redmond OBE for Encountering the Animal – O N C A |url=https://onca.org.uk/conversation-ian-redmond-obe-encountering-animal/ |access-date=2 January 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Awards galore… |url=https://www.orangutan.org.uk/blog/2013/10/25/awards-galore |website=Orangutan Foundation |access-date=2 January 2026 |date=25 October 2013}}</ref>
